newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. declares storm emergency in 25 counties.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. declares storm emergency in 25 counties.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson declared a state of emergency in 25 northern California counties on Thursday because of floods and damage caused by severe winter storms.

Wilson issued the emergency proclamation as much of the northern part of the state was reeling from relentless rain that pushed many rivers to flood stage and caused mudslides, power outages and property damage.
Wilson's emergency proclamation included 25 of the state's 58 counties and covered most of California north of San Francisco.

"These northern California counties have been hard hit by rain and flooding over the past week and they can be assured they have the full support of the state's emergency services," Wilson said in a statement.
"With this declaration, local governments will be eligible for state assistance and financial relief to cover the costs of responding to these acts of mother nature," he added.
The declaration will provide state financial assistance to help repair and rebuild public facilities including sewers, roads, bridges and other public structures.
